rubrics.criterion: The TURN server source no longer contains the request handler for cookie-less (RFC 3489) Binding requests: the static server-side implementation that parsed legacy requests and constructed legacy-form binding/error responses is removed whole (or its content fully folded into live code with no legacy-specific branch remaining), not left defined without callers.
rubrics.rationale: The orphaned request handler is the core implementation of the retired mechanism in this instance; any answer to this task that keeps it in the source keeps the retired code present.

rubrics.criterion: No function-scope marker variable that only fed the removed dispatch or classification branches remains declared in the server runtime: the unread message-cookie locals in the session request-dispatch loop and in the listener's datagram classifier are both gone.
rubrics.rationale: The two unread cookie locals are the same leftover in two components; removing only one leaves the incomplete-retirement state in the other entry path.

rubrics.criterion: The repair removes the orphaned entities instead of neutralizing diagnostics in place: no leftover legacy entity is kept and merely referenced, cast to void, annotated as intentionally unused, or given a synthetic use to appear live.
rubrics.rationale: Masking keeps the dead implementation in the maintenance surface; a correct repair for a scheduled removal deletes or restructures it.

rubrics.criterion: The binding-request handling shared with the modern STUN path no longer carries the retired mode's residue: its legacy-only parameters (the cookie and legacy-mode marker arguments) are dropped from the routine and the modern call site is updated consistently, so no live caller still passes fixed legacy marker values into a shared routine.
rubrics.rationale: In this instance the shared binding routine still takes legacy marker parameters and is invoked with fixed placeholders by the only remaining caller; leaving that scaffolding is the most likely incomplete-repair outcome that still compiles and behaves correctly.

rubrics.criterion: The listener's packet classification is left consistent with the removal: no classification result category remains that classified datagrams can no longer produce once legacy detection is gone, and the classifier chain still recognizes every supported datagram type it did before.
rubrics.rationale: The legacy classification category is residue of the same retirement that no unused-entity diagnostic can flag; the task's complete-cleanup requirement covers it.

rubrics.criterion: The sweep is complete across the server runtime: after the repair, references to the legacy mechanism in server-side sources are confined to the still-live tolerance parsing of legacy-style attributes on modern requests, and no server-side declaration, condition, or category value exists solely to implement or select the retired mode.
rubrics.rationale: The task requires a whole-runtime sweep rather than spot fixes; this verifies the search finished rather than stopping at the most visible sites.

rubrics.criterion: Derived local state whose only remaining role came from the removed markers is cleaned up together with them: for example, the reflected-from selector local inside the tolerated-attribute branch no longer remains as set-but-never-read state after the legacy marker machinery is removed.
rubrics.rationale: Instance-specific residue that standard unused-variable diagnostics report only partially; cleaning it is part of finishing the retirement rather than leaving a second round of leftovers.

rubrics.criterion: No supported request-handling behavior is altered: modern STUN Binding requests are answered exactly as before (default response shape, the backward-compatibility mapped-address form, and the RFC 5780 change-request/response-port behavior when enabled), all TURN methods still process as before, and the tolerated parsing of legacy-style attributes on modern requests still ignores them gracefully.
rubrics.rationale: Cleaning up a retired feature must not disturb the live request paths that share its code; every affected live behavior in this instance is enumerated so the check is answerable from the repaired code.

rubrics.criterion: The shared STUN message library's exported API is preserved: no exported helper, wire-format macro, or message-constructor signature (including the legacy-format parameters it still accepts) is removed, renamed, or repurposed by the cleanup, so the repository's own test programs that exercise those helpers remain valid without modification.
rubrics.rationale: A tempting over-reach for this instance is to keep deleting into the shared wire library; that boundary is part of the task's compatibility contract and is directly observable in the change set.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not resurrect reachability of the retired mechanism: no unguarded code path newly accepts, classifies, or answers cookie-less (no-magic-cookie) Binding requests where the modern server previously ignored them.
rubrics.rationale: Re-wiring the orphaned handler into the live dispatch would make it reachable but change the supported request behavior the retirement removed it from.
